status: REVIEW VARIANT — reconstructed head under the hair and cleaned feature edges on the D-188 baseline; not approved, not promotable

cranium.what: RECONSTRUCTED DESIGN, not observed pixels: one round cranium that continues Northstar's visible face contour above the temples, drawn as its own layer UNDER the D-188 skin layer (the skin layer stays byte-identical).

contour.kind: ellipse arc, mirror-symmetric about the face axis
contour.why: the visible face contour ends at (383, 291) and (637, 291), symmetric about x = 510; the ellipse passes through both points (133.8 · sqrt(1 − (41/130)²) = 127), its slope there (dx/dy ≈ 0.31) continues the face line (≈ 0.2) without a kink, and its top at y = 120 leaves the painted hair (top ≈ 40–60) about 60 px of volume — a design choice, not a measurement

earRootWedges.what: the small skin wedge between each ear's front edge and the face line that the sideburn covered, closed at the top by a short ink stroke from the ear's top corner to the face line

ink.from: the median of the opaque duplicated face-contour ink at the sideburns (D-188 overlap-ink-hair-skin), 319 px

paint.baseFrom: the median of the opaque lit skin of the D-188 skin layer in x 430–590, y 200–300 (10,707 px; the hair's cast shadow is already lifted there)
paint.method: harmonic (Laplace) fill inside a 20 px band next to the visible skin, with the visible skin and the flat base colour beyond the band as fixed boundaries — so the original skin continues into the base colour without a seam. No cel shadow is added: Northstar paints the face itself as flat lit skin.

hairEdgeResidue.what: opaque dark pixels of the D-188 skin layer right next to the hair: the hair's own edge antialias. They move to this variant's hair layer (composite with hair unchanged; the bare head has no dark specks). The face contour's own ink at the join (from y 291 down) is not touched.
hairEdgeResidue.found: 15 px moved (a pre-count with y < 285 found 13; the rule as implemented, rows < 285 inclusive of the 3 px reach, moves 15). The dark px near the hair at y 291–298 are the face contour at the join and stay.

featureEdges.method: LOCAL-INK PROJECTION with the local skin as background. Before it, the hair's own outline that D-188 duplicated into a part (overlap-ink-hair-features, still present in the opaque hair layer) leaves the part. Core = a D-188 part pixel with alpha >= 250 that is darker than the skin under it (luma at least 2 lower) or a white highlight (class W), or a painted shade-fill interior (shadeCores). Every other part pixel is an edge pixel: its local ink K is the colour of the nearest core pixel of the same part (Chebyshev radius <= 4), and its alpha is the projection a = (S − P)·(S − K) / |S − K|², clamped to 0..1, where S is the D-188 reconstructed skin under it and P the original pixel. The pixel becomes K at alpha a (transparent below 0.02). Light sharpening halo next to dark ink projects to a <= 0 and leaves the part (the skin under it is already the reconstructed skin); a highlight's own antialias keeps a white K and stays. Edge pixels with no core within 4 px keep their D-188 value.
featureEdges.shadeCores: painted shade fills are cores too: part pixels with alpha >= 0.3 that are not lighter than the skin, kept where all 8 neighbours are shade (1 px erosion). Added after the first local run turned the nose shadow grey-brown by projecting it onto the dark nose line; the erosion keeps 1–2 px antialias rings out of the cores.
featureEdges.notAppliedTo: the eyes (the pale sclera top inside the eye opening is eye content; the lash's outer edge keeps D-188's lift)

shortHairCoverage.kind: ILLUSTRATIVE COVERAGE MASK, not a hairstyle
